pageTitle: Tell us if you need support
heading: Tell us if you need support

contentBlocks.text: Some people need support to access information and use our services. We call this a reasonable adjustment.
Some examples of reasonable adjustments are:

bullets: bringing support with you to the hearing, like an assistance dog
documents in an alternative format, like large print
regular breaks during a hearing to make you feel more comfortable

contentBlocks.text: You can ask for a reasonable adjustment now by selecting ‘Continue to the questions’, or at any time during your case by selecting ‘Your support’ from your case overview.

Once you’ve submitted your request for support, it’ll be reviewed by the court or a judge. We’ll keep you updated on the status of the request in your account. If we need more information we’ll contact you by the preferred method you’ve already chosen.
You must contact the court directly to ask for something else for you or someone else who’s coming to court to support you.

bullets: communication and documents in Welsh or to speak Welsh at your hearing
special measures, like giving evidence in private, because you’re vulnerable

contentBlocks.text: You can contact the court by email or telephone. You can also visit the court and speak to someone directly.
Use the find a court or tribunal service (opens in new tab) to get your local court’s email address.
If you do not know the name of your local court, select the ‘Money’ category and then the ‘Housing’ category to find it.
Find out about call charges (opens in new tab).
